title: Life of Pompey (Parallel Lives)
author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 87. Trans. Bernadotte Perrin. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 1917. Chapters 1–80. Key chapters: ch. 1–13 (birth, Sulla years, cognomen); ch. 17–22 (Sertorian War); ch. 30–33 (lex Manilia, Mithridatic command); ch. 46–48 (First Triumvirate); ch. 68–73 (Pharsalus); ch. 77–80 (death in Egypt).
note: Key classical biographical source, written ~150 years after events. Moralising but detailed. LCL 87 (Perrin 1917). Reliability: A (primary narrative source; must be corroborated for contested claims).

title: Civil Wars (Bellum Civile), Books 1–5
author: Appian
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 543–544. Trans. Brian McGing. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 2020. (Older edition: LCL 3–5, trans. Horace White, 1913.) Books 2–5 cover Pompey's civil war career, Pharsalus, and death in Egypt.
note: Detailed military narrative of late Republic civil wars. 2nd century CE. LCL 543–544 (McGing 2020) is the current preferred edition. Reliability: A (well-sourced narrative; cross-check against Plutarch and Dio).

title: Roman History, Books 36–42
author: Cassius Dio
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 53 (Books 36–40, trans. Earnest Cary, 1914) and LCL 66 (Books 41–45, trans. Earnest Cary, 1916). Cambridge: Harvard University Press. Books 36–42 cover Pompey's prime years (Third Mithridatic War through Pharsalus).
note: Books 36–42 cover Pompey's career. 3rd century CE. LCL 53 and LCL 66 (Cary 1914–1916). Reliability: A (comprehensive but late; sometimes conflates traditions; corroborate with Plutarch and Appian).

title: Commentarii de Bello Civili (Civil War), Books 1–3
author: Julius Caesar
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 39. Trans. Cynthia Damon. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 2016. (Earlier edition: trans. A. G. Peskett, 1914.) Books 1–3 cover the civil war of 49–48 BCE; Book 3 includes Pharsalus and events up to Pompey's departure to Egypt.
note: First-person account by Caesar of the civil war; obviously pro-Caesar. Primary source for 49–48 BCE. LCL 39 (Damon 2016 is preferred revised edition). Reliability: A (eyewitness military operations; bias must be noted for political claims).

title: Life of Crassus (Parallel Lives)
author: Plutarch
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 65. Trans. Bernadotte Perrin. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 1916. Key chapters for Pompey: ch. 11–13 (Spartacus; rivalry with Pompey); ch. 14–15 (joint consulship 70 BCE); ch. 36–38 (Luca conference 56 BCE; Crassus's death 53 BCE and its impact on triumvirate).
note: Plutarch's Life of Crassus provides context for Pompey-Crassus rivalry including Spartacus episode and First Triumvirate. LCL 65 (Perrin 1916). Reliability: A (parallel to Life of Pompey; same methodological caveats apply).

title: Pro Lege Manilia (De Imperio Cn. Pompei)
author: Cicero
citation_detail: Loeb Classical Library 198. Trans. H. Grose Hodge. Cambridge: Harvard University Press, 1927. Speech delivered 66 BCE supporting Pompey's Mithridatic command. Sections 27–50 praise Pompey's qualities and military achievements.
note: Contemporary 66 BCE speech supporting Pompey's command against Mithridates. LCL 198 (Hodge 1927). Reliability: A (contemporary eyewitness political rhetoric; note: laudatory purpose means selectivity).
